Use case: stylized-concept. Runtime pixel-inspired sprite atlas, NOT a scene or mockup. Reference images are style/identity references only, not edit targets. Make a portrait atlas with EXACTLY 4 equal columns and EXACTLY 5 equal rows, 20 distinct full-body sprites total. Each cell contains one complete character, no duplicates overlapping neighboring cells. Fixed elevated 3/4 top-down game camera, camera never rotates or tilts; character turns within that fixed camera. Row 1 SOUTH: character faces down toward viewer, frontal face visible. Row 2 SOUTHEAST: character faces lower-right, right frontal 3/4. Row 3 EAST: character faces screen-right in side profile, head and feet oriented right. Row 4 NORTHEAST: character faces upper-right AWAY from viewer, rear 3/4, back of hood/coat visible, face mostly hidden. Row 5 NORTH: character faces straight up AWAY from viewer, direct back view, NO face, cloak and back of hood visible. These five directions must truly differ anatomically, never rotate the bitmap in-plane. Identical silhouette scale, anatomy and costume across all 20 cells. Body occupies 68% of cell height (head to soles, exclude sword). Each character's foot anchor at x=50%, y=87% inside its cell, identical across every frame, no translation between frames. Keep whole weapon inside cell with at least 6% transparent gutters. Crisp dark outline and chunky pixel shading, restrained teal/ivory/steel/gold palette, warm lighting from top-left. Truly transparent RGBA background. NO background glow, NO brown backdrop, NO floor, NO drop shadow, NO numbers, NO row labels, NO text, NO grid lines.
Subject: the exact same human beast hunter from reference: teal blue hood and scarf, ivory fur coat tails and collar, dark steel plated armor with thin gold edges, leather belt, single oversized silver serrated greatsword with gold hilt. Do not change his outfit, weapon or body proportions.
Animation: Each row is a 4-frame LOOPING WALK: column 1 left leg forward/right leg back, column 2 passing feet, column 3 right leg forward/left leg back, column 4 passing feet with opposite arm motion. Keep sword lowered and carried in the right hand, not swinging. Clear alternating leg movement and cloak movement, no sliding body translation.

Layout correction:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit target: this 20-sprite atlas. Preserve the exact hunter identity, all 5 direction views, and each existing articulated animation pose. Change ONLY sprite arrangement, spacing and consistent scale. Re-layout into EXACTLY 4 columns by 5 rows of equally-sized cells with LARGE empty transparent gutters BETWEEN all sprites. Every entire sprite including the full sword, cloak, feet and raised weapon must fit in just the central 60% of its cell, leaving at least 20% empty TRANSPARENT padding on all four sides. No blade, cape, leg or head may cross into another cell's area, even during the contact and raised-sword frames. Shrink sprites consistently to create room, do not crop or shorten swords. Keep identical anatomical body size and foot baseline in each row and between rows. Keep row order SOUTH front, SOUTHEAST front-right, EAST right profile, NORTHEAST rear-right, NORTH back. Keep original palette, pixel brushwork and dark outlines. Truly transparent RGBA, NO new background, NO shadows, NO colored haze, NO text or labels, NO lines. It is essential to leave visible transparent blank gaps separating every sprite on all sides.
